phases.journal: Somebody is ring-barking the oldest cedars of the Rainwood and felling them by night. The feller at the Sound cut wants wolves to sit up in the stands.

effects.text: Mind the old stand. The best cedars in the Rainwood are dying on their feet, and I can't stand guard on every tree.

phases.journal: The night crews are broken, and the tow-rope led to a Grayrock slipway. What is a cedar worth?

effects.text: We know whose saws, now. A shipwright on the Wharf. What's a cedar worth to her, and what's it worth to us?

triggers.note: The tally: the road with the most weight; a tie goes to the contract; nobody: the cedars are taken.

effects.text: A mast a season, felled by our own axes and paid to our own stores. The Sisters stand. I can live with that bargain.

effects.text: The cedars went home up the Sound. I'd have given a week's pay to see the faces on the Wharf.
The cedars came home up the Sound. Root and rain, the Wharf will think twice.

phases.journal: Nobody stood up for the cedars. The night crews took more of the Sisters, and they will be back.

effects.text: Three more Sisters down. Nobody stopped them. I've stopped counting the stumps.

quests.title: Ring-Barked
quests.summary: Somebody is killing the old cedars of the Rainwood. Walk the stands and find out who.

offer.say: #greet#, #address#. Somebody's ring-barking the old cedars. A band of bark cut right round, so the tree dies on its feet and nobody asks why it's felled after. Five gone from the old stand already. Walk the stands and find me who.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. That's a shipwright's knot. Nobody ties a log like that to burn it. They're masts, then. They're stealing masts. Come back with a pack and we'll sit up in the stands.
